summary: The frame of a step-by-step explanation: the caller draws the explanation (in the `content` slot) from the current step, and the walkthrough shows that step's title and text, "Step N of M" with dots, Back and Next (Done on the last step), and optionally a play / pause button that advances one step every `interval` seconds. It publishes the live step and an eased copy of it for the drawing.

titles.doc: One title per step, in order, e.g. ["Lift", "Release", "Swing"]; fixed when the document is built. Shown above the step's text and announced as "Step N of M: <title>"

texts.doc: One explanation per step (same order as titles). Long texts wrap; give `captionHeight` so the drawing keeps its size from step to step. Omit it for titles only

count.doc: Number of steps; by default the number of titles

step.doc: The step, 0-based, which Back, Next and Pause write. Bind a document variable ("@step") to set it from the host; unbound, the call keeps its own. While autoplay plays, this variable stays where play started: read `shown` for the step on screen

shown.doc: Publishes the step on screen (the step, or the timed one while playing) under the name of the variable you bind ("@stepNow"): a tree variable written at the walkthrough's head, so read it in the `content` slot, or anywhere after the walkthrough in the document. Do NOT also declare it in resources (an earlier reader would get that 0). Unbound: unused

eased.doc: Publishes `shown` eased over 0.6 s (the standard cubic curve) under the name you bind ("@stepEased"): it glides from 1 to 2 when the step changes, so a drawing can morph between steps with clamp or lerp over it. Same rules as `shown`. Mono: it is the step itself (no motion)

autoplay.doc: true adds a play / pause button: playing advances one step every `interval` seconds from the step on screen and stops on the last one (then play starts over). Not in mono (no motion on e-ink and always-on displays)

playing.doc: 1 while playing. Bind a document variable to read it, or pass 1 to start playing when the document loads ("playing": 1); unbound, the call keeps its own

captionHeight.doc: Fixed height of the title and text area in dp; 0 sizes it to the current step's text, so the controls (and a `content` above them) move when the text length changes

doneLabel.doc: Label of the button that replaces Next on the last step: "Done" when onDone is given, else "Start over"

color.doc: Next / Done and the current dot

onStep.doc: Actions run after Back and after Next change the step (valueFloatChange, ...). For a hostNamedAction use onNext / onBack instead: a named action written in two click lists reaches the host by name from one of them only

onNext.doc: Actions run on Next, after the step changes, e.g. [{"type": "hostNamedAction", "name": "next"}]

onBack.doc: Actions run on Back, after the step changes

onDone.doc: Actions run by the last step's button (a hostNamedAction closing the explanation, ...). Omitted: that button reads Start over and goes back to step 1

loop.doc: With autoplay: after the last step play goes on from the first (a cycle: an engine, a heartbeat, the seasons) until paused, instead of stopping at the end

content.doc: The explanation itself (a canvas, any layout), above the caption, filling the height the walkthrough leaves: it reads the variables bound to `shown` and `eased`. Without it the walkthrough is only its caption and controls

texts: Pull the bob to one side.
Let go: gravity pulls it down.
It swings past the middle and up the other side.

pitfalls: For a new explainer use StepExplainer: it adapts to size, has its own background, and takes computed step counts and captions. Walkthrough has a fixed count and static captions

The drawing must read `shown` or `eased`, not `step`: while autoplay plays, `step` stays where play started and the step on screen is computed from the clock. Pause, Back and Next write the step on screen back into `step`, so a paused walkthrough has step = shown

`shown` and `eased` are published as tree variables named after the variables you bind ({"$name": ...}): read them in the `content` slot or anywhere after the call in the document. Never declare them in resources as well: the resources variable wins and reads 0 (check_component's demo declares every @name a call references, so a sweep of a call whose content reads @stepEased draws step 0; check the drawing with the document instead). A reader before the call fails to convert (Variable not found)

Grow the k-th element of a drawing with clamp(0, 1, @stepEased - (k - 1)) (0 before step k, 1 after, easing in between), and fade its labels with the same value as paint alpha. Keep the drawing's own canvas variables out of resources too

Autoplay reads animationTime() (seconds since the player started the document), not the wall clock: shown = clamp(0, last, step + playing × (s0 + floor((animationTime() − t0) / interval) − step)). Play runs five actions in order: step = shown, step = 0 if not running and on the last step (play there starts over), s0 = step, t0 = animationTime(), playing = 1 − running. Running is playing × (shown < last), so the button shows Play again on the last step

No clock listener: frames while playing come from an animated local whose target, running × floor(animationTime() × 2), changes every half second (each change restarts a 0.75 s ease), so a PLAYING walkthrough repaints every frame and a paused or finished one is idle (inspect runtime: idle). check_component's lint warning "animationTime() alone never schedules a repaint" is expected: that local is what schedules it. A continuousSec() clock would keep the document repainting even while paused (TIM-14)

Playing does not survive a reload: t0 is relative to the player's animationTime, so a document reloaded with playing 1 times its steps from the load. Pass "playing": 1 to start playing at load; the first step comes after `interval`. A timed step runs no action and tells the host nothing: onStep, onNext and onBack run on taps only
Mono (mono-dark, mono-light) has no play button and no autoplay (no motion on e-ink or always-on displays), and `eased` is `shown` itself: the drawing snaps

The step on screen is clamp(0, last, round(step)): a host value out of range shows the first or last step. The caption is one text per title and per text, each with an exact 0/1 visibility 1 − min(1, |shown − i|); the title is announced "Step N of M: <title>" and the text after it. The "Step N of M" line is drawn on the progress canvas, so a screen reader does not hear it twice

With a `content` slot the walkthrough fills its parent (fillMaxSize) and the content takes the height the caption and controls leave: give it a parent with a height. Without `captionHeight` the caption takes the current step's height and everything above and below moves when the text length changes; with it, a longer text is clipped

Back is a Button with a runtime enabled (min(1, shown)), dimmed and inert on step 1. Next and the last step's button are two Buttons switched by visibility; the last one runs onDone, or without it reads Start over and goes back to step 1. A tap on Back or Next while playing stops playing. Every target is 48 dp tall
Give a hostNamedAction to onNext / onBack / onDone, never to onStep: a named action written in two click lists reaches the host by name from one of them only (Stepper)

A document variable named `step` hides the step() function in your own expressions (json2rc resolves the bare token as the variable, so step(x, e) becomes nonsense); this component avoids step() for that reason. Use min/max arithmetic, or name the variable otherwise
The dots are 7 dp at a 14 dp pitch, right-aligned, decorative (not tappable); past about 12 steps they crowd the "Step N of M" line
inspect pins animationTime() to its clock (seconds since 2026-01-01, which loses sub-second precision as a float): pin clock "2026-01-01T00:00:00" when checking autoplay with inspect interact

Expanded, never a pattern: it contains texts (U7) and declares named values. Each instance costs about 3.7 KB with three short steps and autoplay (3.0 KB without autoplay; mono about 3.8 KB, no play button) plus about 350 B per further step and the length of its strings, mostly in the three Buttons (Back has two faces for its runtime enabled)
loop: the eased step (eased) runs back from the last step to the first when the cycle wraps; a drawing that must jump forward at the wrap reads shown (the whole step) and its own phase
